Episode 209. The Seventh Tomb of Temar - Kaitam's Painting (1)
"What? What do you mean there are guardians inside?"
"That's right. Since it's a painting originally intended for a tomb, wouldn't that be a natural assumption?"

"Neither the fact that there's a space inside the painting, nor that there are guardians inside, nor that the strength of these guardians is up to the painter's whimsy is 'natural' at all. How strong are these guardians?"
"I can't recall their exact capabilities. As I said earlier, my memory has been compromised due to the damage to the painting. But all I can say is that they are incredibly powerful."
"You're not saying that there are guardians with the strength equivalent to that of a Star Eater?"
"I don't think so. That would be a breach of consistency... since there was no one stronger than them among the people of Temar at that time."
"What about me?"
"I'm well aware that it would have been difficult to determine superiority between you and Temar. Ah, then I might have portrayed you at your peak."
"If it's my peak, even if the kid and I attack together, we won't stand a chance."
"Really? Is it that serious? I thought you said you were close to your prime."

"Close and complete are different. Heh heh, back then, this Murakan, well, let's just say that if it wasn't a Star Eater, it couldn't kill me, no matter how many strong guys swarmed me, if there wasn't a Star Eater among them, they couldn't kill me."
"Sounds like bluffing."
"If you think it's bluffing, you become a Star Eater. Then again, what would you know, kid? You'd have to become a Star Eater to understand. Kya kya kya."
Jin was about to throw a punch.
"……Fortunately, everything I've painted can only exist within the painting. Whether there's a peak Murakan inside, or something even stronger, it's impossible for them to come out."
If Kaitam had been able to bring his paintings to reality, he wouldn't have been regarded as a lower-middle class god.
"However, if you enter my painting, that place will become your reality during that time. You can be injured by the guardians' attacks. Therefore, if you can't beat them, it means you could die."
"So, if I understand you correctly, Kaitam... The painting contains a piece of history from a thousand years ago, but there are no other rewards, and it's full of immeasurable dangers."
Kaitam nodded awkwardly. He felt he couldn't argue if Jin and Murakan refused to enter the painting.
But Jin had no intention of giving up.
He believed it was worth risking the danger if he could directly verify a piece of complete history from a thousand years ago.
Furthermore, the painting began to be contaminated 'suddenly', and Kaitam said that the likelihood of it being due to historical manipulation was slim.
Witch Helluram, or Lokia Ganesto.
Jin had a feeling that this incident was somehow related to them.

'But if one of them is the culprit, I don't know why they would suddenly damage Kaitam's painting now. Because they don't want me to know the history depicted in the painting? Then there would have been a better time than now. When I didn't have enough strength to help Kaitam.'
The reason why the suspects damaged the painting would only be known once they entered it.
"Kaitam, is there any safety measure for entering the painting? Like a way to escape immediately."
"Since I lost control of the painting, I'd have to say there's no such thing for now. However, you may regain control if you manage to repair the damaged paintings inside."
"So, basically, you're asking us to restore the painting?"

"I can't argue with that interpretation, Murakan. But I sincerely think that you guys need to look into the stories from that era. In the first place, no one else can enter unless they can handle the spirit energy. The restoration of the artwork is just my wish. Even if you safely explore what happened a thousand years ago and return, there is a high possibility that my painting will not be restored."
"Ah, why are you taking a joke so seriously? Are you really sorry?"
"Of course."
"Really?"
"Yes!"
"So, can I interpret this as you would accept any compensation I ask for?"
"Uh, I am sorry, but when you say it like that, it seems my rationality is somewhat compromised. Krrrrrr..."

"Kaitam is thinking about us and asked us to go in. What more compensation do you need, Murakan? We might find an important clue about a thousand years ago. That's the biggest reward. It's history you don't remember either."
"No, no. But maybe thanks to us, the painting can be restored. I have something I must ask of this painter."
"Stop being annoying and just say it. What is it?"
"Draw me a collection of erotic pictures. A collection drawn by the painter himself, kya......Amazing. I'll be able to fix my ruined eyes because of Ruet."
"I'm amazed, Murakan. Are you asking a god for something like that?"
"Alright, I'll draw it. Jin, if you have a picture you want to request from me, tell me."
"I'm grateful for the offer."
"Hehe, then I'll take the kid's part too."
"I'll think about it after we get back. It'll definitely be something more valuable than erotic pictures."
"Can't stand seeing me succeed, can you? Tsk. This little guy had his cute moments when he was a child."
"We'll enter the painting now, Master Keitam."
Despite the fact there was virtually no safety mechanism, Jin wasn't burdened or scared.

'Since Keitam mentioned there would be no God-Beasts due to coherence, there should be no enemies that Murakan and I can't handle now. The variable that Prime Murakan may exist is there, but... after all, it's a painting. It must be different from a real God-Beast.'
Even if the scale of power was the same, it didn't mean the painting would have the same combat power as a God-Beast. No matter how lifelike, a painting is a painting; there must be a limit.

If a being identical to the God-Beast of reality could be depicted at will, then Keitam's painting would have been the final tomb of Tamer. There would be no need to perform such a ritual with such guardians.
"Understood. Ox, Telpen!"

Ox and Telpen approached. Ox surrounded the easel with a translucent border, and Telpen took a pencil out of his mouth and handed it to Keitam. The pencil grew to the size of a spear as soon as it touched Keitam's hand.

"I'm going to draw a passage into the painting. Everyone needs to be as still as death. This requires extreme concentration. Especially you, Murakan. Don't open the door like before. It annoys me thinking you might interrupt my work."
"Well, okay..."
"I told you to shut up!"

This time, both Jin and Murakan were silent, somewhat taken aback. Keitam was already brandishing the enormous pencil over the black canvas. His eyes, filled with madness, flickered brightly. Murakan wound his index finger around his hair, and Jin shrugged his shoulders.
As the pencil moved, a white, round circle began to form on the black painting. After a moment, a landscape began to emerge within the white circle.
'... A forest? No, a mountain?'

The circle was too small to clearly see the landscape, but it was clear that it was full of green trees. It felt like looking down at a forest or mountain through a small gap in the clouds. The scale was obviously huge at first glance.
Drip, drip.
Keitam's sweat drops fell to the floor. He sat down as if he was done, wiping his forehead.
"Whew, I barely opened it. Almost didn't make it."
"The tomb looks more like a forest. It seems to be part of a massive mountain range. Is the tomb located somewhere there?"

"Probably? Damn, I don't even remember what the landscape of my work looks like. I don't know how to express this awful feeling. You guys go and let me know. If it's restored, I'll draw over a hundred volumes of Spring Paintings. Please! God! Give me an answer!"
You are the god, aren't you? Besides, over a hundred volumes!?

Jin naturally thought Murakan would scream and make a fuss, so he instinctively covered his ears. But Murakan was staring intently into the circle. His eyes were trembling as if he had received a shock.
"Murakan?"
"That's... my, my mountain range..."
"Your... mountain range?"
"Yes, my mountain range, my home. I can tell just by looking at those trees... it's definitely the Murakan mountain range."
Mount Murakan.
The highest mountain on earth, its name naturally derived from Murakan, who was the master of the mountain.
And now, Murakan was experiencing a flood of memories from a time he had forgotten.

Memories of when Mount Murakan wasn't just a 'mountain' but a 'mountain range' that spanned the entire Huphester. At that time, the Murakan range was called the backbone of Huphester, and Murakan was its sole ruler.
"Are you saying that Mount Murakan used to be a mountain range?"
"Yes... what remains now is what was left after everything broke down back then. The storm castle at the top as well... Ugh!"
Suddenly, Murakan clutched his forehead and doubled over.
"Murakan, are you okay?"

"I'm fine. Damn, every time I remember that period, a headache comes on. I don't know how I've managed to forget about my massive mountain range for so long. The central part was in Mitel, and it spanned the entire Huphester region. From the southernmost point to the northernmost point."
"You're saying such a massive mountain range existed in Huphester?"
"Yes. There wasn't a dragon that could pass through that mountain range without my permission."
Even after a thousand years, there should have been stories about such a massive mountain range.
Nothing about the Murakan mountain range was recorded in history books, and there were no oral stories.
There was only one old legend left in Runcandel.
After the black dragon Murakan was defeated by the first family head, Temar Runcandel, a thousand years ago, he gave him the storm castle and fell into a deep sleep.
Jin was overwhelmed by intuition.
'The story from a thousand years ago that Master Kaytam captured in the painting is probably the truth about Murakan and Temar...'
Murakan took a deep breath and raised his head.
"So, Mr. Kaytam. How do we get in now?"
[If you push your head in, you'll slip right in like you missed a step. It looks like you've already started to recover some old memories.]
"It's not just some, I need to get all of them back. Don't forget about those hundred volumes of Chunhwa. Let's go, kiddo."
